free_tier.stated: No published byte quota. The platform documents hosting over 5 petabytes of data across 330+ products from 130+ organizations, serving approximately 700 TB per month for public data publishing. Documentation specifies no per-product, per-account, or per-file cap.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered in practice for the reader: anonymous GET with no credentials, Cloudflare in front, R2/Turbo-adjacent CDN headers. No egress meter appears anywhere in the docs.

record.tooling: Genuine S3 proxy. Endpoint https://data.source.coop, --no-sign-request for reads. Upload credentials are Source-issued but in AWS format and valid only at the proxy; path is s3://<account-id>/<product-id>/ and you cannot write outside your own prefix. Accepts aws cli, boto3, rclone with a custom endpoint, plus a Source CLI and service accounts for CI.
record.chaining: Multiplier is data products per account/org, and orgs can hold team members. Because reads are anonymous and S3-native, this is the cleanest 'someone else's S3 on a real CDN' shape in the whole D area. It can be mounted by AList/rclone and fronted by Cloudflare exactly per §2.1.
record.limits_note: Write-gated. Publishing data requires application to the beta testing program via web form. Future flat pricing is announced for upcoming release. Data repositories are public by default with no private mode.
record.reliability_note: Beta + announced-but-unpublished pricing means the free window has an unknown end date. Store only data that has a second home.

evidence.proved: PROBED (this is the new evidence): curl -qsS -D - -> HTTP 200, Content-Length: 16187, Accept-Ranges: bytes, ETag, Last-Modified, Server: cloudflare, CF-Cache-Status: DYNAMIC. Downloaded twice and SHA-256 compared: cdd18d37e1af2320c2eaa763a6b70a8258a1ee2e5dc78e558ea0922e981e56d6 on both copies, and 16,187 bytes on disk matches the declared Content-Length — a true roundtrip, not a 200-with-empty-body.
PROBED: curl -H 'Range: bytes=0-99' on the same object -> HTTP 206 Partial Content, Content-Range: bytes 0-99/16187, 100 bytes body. Range requests work, so resumable/parallel fetches are viable.

record.provider: Source Cooperative - uncapped public publishing, beta-gated

free_tier.stated: No published byte cap: 'allowing trusted organizations and individuals to publish data of any kind at any scale'. Case study: Earth Genome publishes 60+ TB. Platform total reported at just over 5 PB.

egress.terms: Free public reads through the data proxy at data.source.coop - live probe returned HTTP 200 with Cloudflare in front (CF-RAY present), so reads are CDN-covered.

record.tooling: Objects served at data.source.coop/<account>/<product>/...; the proxy is open source (Rust, github.com/source-cooperative/data.source.coop). Bring Your Own Bucket (BYOB) points Source at an S3 bucket you own, read via OIDC federation (sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity) with no long-lived secret either side.
record.chaining: Per data product, owned by 'an organization or an individual' explicitly. BYOB is the important primitive: it decouples the catalogue/CDN from the bytes, so a free bucket elsewhere becomes a Source product with Cloudflare-fronted reads.
record.limits_note: Beta: publishing requires acceptance as a beta tester via a Google Form, and BYOB requires Source staff to enable it per account ('contact hello@source.coop'). Public-only by design - 'all data hosted in Source is available to the public'. New products default to Unlisted.
record.reliability_note: Nonprofit (Radiant Earth 501(c)(3) parent) with in-kind AWS/Azure; beta terms can change. Storage itself lives on commodity cloud, so durability is AWS-grade.
